# Harriet Ainslie

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss Ainslie  <sub>[v5 c4 P50](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0050), [v5 c4 P53](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0053)</sub>; Miss Harriet  <sub>[v5 c4 P53](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0053), [v5 c4 P54](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0054), [v5 c12 P5](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Harriet is dark and large of build, standing ten years older than her sister Clementine. She has black hair, bushy black eyebrows, and eyes matching the transparent, slaty blue of gulf waters during a northerly breeze. Although her expression often appears somewhat severe and off-putting, she looks quite handsome in her stern, dark-eyebrowed manner.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P54](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0054), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 c22 P8](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0008)_

## Personality

Despite her intimidating exterior, Harriet possesses a cheerful disposition marked by a robust laugh and an agreeable, deep voice. She is an avid reader interested in global affairs and politics, possessing a sharp intellect and a keen sense of humor. She is straightforward, honest, and free of small-mindedness or neighborhood malice. However, she can also be fiercely determined, possessive of her domestic routine, and terrified of loneliness.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P54](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0054), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 c21 P8](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0008), [v5 c21 P10](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0010), [v5 c21 P13](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0013), [v5 c22 P3](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0003), [v5 c22 P22](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0022), [v5 c22 P30](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0030)_

## History

Harriet Ainslie grew up in a strict Episcopalian family. In her youth, she was courted for two years by Lionel Fairlie until a foolish disagreement caused him to marry Dinah Coyle out of spite. Following her mother's death when Clementine was twenty-five, Harriet was overcome by grief and horror at the thought of being left alone, leading her to demand a mutual vow with Clementine upon their mother's Bible to never marry. When John Ashdown began visiting their house and fell in love with Clementine, Harriet frequently engaged him in lively debates on world affairs while keeping a close eye on their interactions to enforce the vow. Upon learning that Ashdown proposed to Clementine, Harriet adamantly refused to release her sister from her oath. Later, after reconnecting with Lionel Fairlie, Harriet found herself courted by him once more. Realizing she wished to marry Lionel, Harriet felt bound by her own logic, eventually consenting to let Clementine marry Ashdown as well.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 c13 P27](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0027), [v5 c13 P29](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0029), [v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 c21 P10](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0010), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 c21 P20](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0020), [v5 c21 P24](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0024), [v5 c22 P1](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0001), [v5 c22 P22](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0022), [v5 c22 P28](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0028), [v5 c26 P15](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0015), [v5 c32 P22](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0022), [v5 c34 P43](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0043), [v5 c35 P7](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0007)_

## Background by volume

- Her father died when she was thirteen years old.  <sub>[v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015)</sub>
- Her younger brother passed away when he was twelve.  <sub>[v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015)</sub>
- In her youth, she had a romance with Lionel Fairlie that abruptly ended in a dispute.  <sub>[v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015)</sub>
- Following her mother's death, she made Clementine swear a solemn oath over their mother's Bible that neither of them would ever marry.  <sub>[v5 c21 P17](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0017), [v5 c21 P20](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0020), [v5 c21 P23](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0023), [v5 c21 P24](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0024)</sub>

## Quotes

> God bless you, no, it has not. Not a day passes without people and countries acting foolishly and resorting to fighting. We are not that close to the millennium, Mr. Ashdown, a fact you realize just as well as I.  <sub>[v5 c13 P29](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0029)</sub>

> You will not belong to me forever. After getting married, you will go away from me. Only I will remain, entirely by myself. It is impossible for me to endure that idea—simply impossible. Passing away would be my preference.  <sub>[v5 c21 P20](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0020)</sub>

> Do you solemnly give me your promise on that? Swear it using mother’s Bible.  <sub>[v5 c21 P23](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0023)</sub>

> I shall refrain from doing it. To me, a pledge remains a pledge. I shall refrain from doing it. Violate your own word—commit perjury if you so choose—yet it will occur without any agreement from me.  <sub>[v5 c22 P28](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0028)</sub>
